why: Both concern April Fools claims, but one is staged inside the room and the other tests outside claims.

why.T3-011: Concepts are a call to help r/DetroitLions finish a helmet and a report that the Lions target is finished, i.e. sending help to another room's work rather than trading or asking for help.

why.T3-028: The item centers on making, sharing, editing, debugging and running scripts to rebuild the Wheel after the first attempt fails; relocation and recruiting are in service of the scripted build.

why.T3-029: The concepts voice loss of the first Wheel: a pseudo-victory after it is gone and mourning as another civilization occupies its ruins.

why.T3-001: Members stage/reveal April Fools fakes (Blackhawks switch, Zetterberg retirement) and others fall for or play along.
why.T3-032: Three or more concepts object to the sub's April Fools content as going too far, annoying, or unwelcome in a news sub, and ask for limits.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-001 carries the staged fake and reactions to it but not the distinct objecting practice that asks the jokes stop or be off-limits.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0343426, C0670580 and C1532337 are objections to the April Fools content, and C0585942 asks Zetterberg be off limits for the jokes.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-032 if forced to one; the loss is the sub's objections and requests to limit the jokes.

why.T3-050: The single concept is a taunt at r/DetroitLions as the Titans' official sub, i.e. mockery of a rival community rather than an attack or ethnic joke.

why.T3-010: The item is dominated by settling borders, overlaps, shifts and space with neighbouring works, e.g. UK border messages, mutual noninterference, overlap fixes with Mariners/TransFlagPlace/McGill/Buffalo.

why.T3-042: The concepts put upkeep and completion of the Winged Wheel before side fights, trolling other teams, or spending scarce resources on other projects.

why.T3-011: Concepts are a call to help r/DetroitLions finish a helmet and a report that the Lions target is finished, i.e. sending help to another room's work rather than trading or asking for help.

why.T3-075: The single concept objects to repeated r/place threads and asks people to stop making them, i.e. objecting to the canvas flood rather than moderating it or judging the canvas.

why.T3-073: The concepts recount how the completed Wheel was made and what happened: hours of coordination, relocation, bot-making, and the shared canvas context for that account.

why.T3-022: The item responds to the reported loss of the Wheel by finding and moving to a new location, with calls to take back or stay as surrounding reactions.

why.T3-038: The concepts coordinate the manual build itself: target/template, outline and fill sequence, first squares, borders, instructions and progress reports.

why.T3-009: Concepts celebrate the finished Wheel as achieved: beautiful, we did it, love the logo, and r/place over with thanks.
why.T3-021: Many concepts are upkeep/repair after completion: repairs around stripe, rebuilding wing, maintaining old school, fixing logo.
why.T3-028: Concepts keep, switch off, or stop trusting scripts for maintaining the Wheel.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009 carries the celebration but not the distinct ongoing repair and upkeep that continues after the work is called done.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0934334, C0416382, C0884984 and C1334044 are repair/rebuild instructions and calls, satisfying T3-021's maintenance gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-021 if forced to one; the loss is the post-celebration repair and upkeep.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009 and T3-021 do not carry the script-specific practice of keeping, stopping trust in, or switching off scripts for maintenance.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1249469, C0358961, C0670684 and C0854666 keep or switch off scripts to maintain the logo.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-028 if forced to one; the loss is script-based maintenance.

why.T3-027: The item argues whether scripts and bots are fair: cheating accusations, warnings of bans, distinctions from timer-bypassing scripts, and defences of bots as public self-preservation.
